mathematicalReview.obligation: arbitrary subset to fixed-cardinality sorted window
mathematicalReview.reason: If an arbitrary k-element solution exists, minimum k-sum S0<=u and maximum k-sum S_last>=l. Consecutive k-window sums are nondecreasing and grow by at most global spread<=u-l. Either S0 already meets the range or the first window crossing l cannot jump above u. For spread0 all k-window sums coincide, so the same conclusion holds.

Discard a start only when its sum through the current right endpoint exceeds u. Positive future elements can never make that start valid again. After shrinking, any shorter suffix has no greater sum; when retained sum<l none of these suffixes can be valid. Thus every contiguous solution is retained until found.

The sorted entries pair each weight with its unique original index. A contiguous slice therefore returns distinct original positions whose actual sum is the tracked sum. Absence of every contiguous solution excludes arbitrary solutions by the fixed-cardinality lemma. With l>=1 the empty vector is unambiguously no solution.

Width is essential for this normal-form claim. Positive counterexamples [1,2,4] target5,[2,3,7] target9,[3,4,9] target12,[4,7,13] target17 have an arbitrary first+last subset but no sorted contiguous solution; all correctly reject at the API width validation. The monotone discard proof relies on positive weights, which are all checked before sorting.

implementationReview.genericApi: template signed integral Weight of size<=int64, optional<vector<int>> find_subset_in_range(int64,int64,span<const Weight>)
implementationReview.emptyExtension: N0 accepted for valid lower/upper,returns nullopt;source N>=1 subset preserved
implementationReview.validation: N<=200000,1<=lower<=upper<=INT32_MAX,all weights1..INT32_MAX,and width>=spread checked before sort/search allocations. Invalid trailing values are not skipped by an early successful search. Empty successful answer impossible.
implementationReview.types: int64 sum and signed64 range values; signed char/short/int/int64 span overloads tested; unsigned and floating element types rejected at compile time. Original input signed-int type follows the source language mapping.
implementationReview.numericProof: After each right iteration sum<=upper. Adding one legal weight gives sum<=2*INT32_MAX; it may overflow int32 but fits int64. Lower/upper validation precedes subtraction, so width and max-min fit int64. left can become right+1 only when current sum=0,which cannot pass the positive-lower success branch; right-left+1 is formed only for a nonempty found slice.
implementationReview.state: No mutable global/static state in production. Const input span and by-value original adapters preserve caller inputs. Results own their storage. Sort order pairs weight with original index for deterministic equal values. All allocations use RAII and exceptions propagate.
implementationReview.complexity: O(N log(N+1)) total time,O(N) auxiliary/output storage plus sort O(log N) call stack; no search depends on the ~2.1e9 bound. Empty case O(1). Input scans and window moves are linear; each endpoint moves forward at most N times.
implementationReview.resourceInterpretation: Recorded timings/RSS include driver oracles and sanitizer overhead and are observed,not universal1second guarantees. Original1s/2GB facts and asymptotic/64bit proofs are separately checked.
